title: Minimum wage increase on restaurant employment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two–way‐fixed‐effects Difference-in-Differences (DID).  
Why: We observe treated and control restaurants before and after the state raises its minimum wage in quarter 4. A DID with unit and time fixed effects isolates the average change in log employment that is unique to treated units in the post period.  

Key assumptions  
• Parallel trends: In the absence of the wage hike, employment at treated and control restaurants would have evolved in parallel.  
• No spill-overs: Control-state restaurants are not affected by the treated state’s higher wage.  
• Stable composition: No systematic entry/exit correlated with treatment.  

A dynamic event-study (leads/lags) is added as a robustness check of the parallel-trends assumption.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ================================================================
# Minimum-wage DID on fast-food restaurant employment
# ================================================================
# Required packages
library(tidyverse)   # data handling
library(fixest)      # high-performance FE regressions
library(modelsummary) # nice tables (optional)

# 1. Read data ----------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s02_data.csv"
df   <- read_csv(path,
                 col_types = cols(
                   unit_id      = col_integer(),
                   period       = col_integer(),
                   treated      = col_integer(),
                   post         = col_integer(),
                   treat_x_post = col_integer(),
                   y            = col_double()
                 ))

# 2. Baseline DID -------------------------------------------------
did_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                 data    = df,
                 cluster = "unit_id")   # cluster at restaurant level

cat("\n=== Baseline DID result ===\n")
print(coeftable(did_mod, se = "cluster")["treat_x_post", ])

# 3. Event-study (leads/lags) ------------------------------------
# Treat quarter 4 as the event time (t = 0)
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(rel_time = period - 4)   # −3,…,0,…,4
# Estimate dynamic effects; omit −1 as the reference period
event_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) |
                     unit_id + period,
                   data    = df,
                   cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n=== Event-study DID (selected leads/lags) ===\n")
# Display coefficients in tidy form
event_tbl <- broom::tidy(event_mod) %>% 
  filter(str_detect(term, "rel_time")) %>% 
  select(term, estimate, std.error, p.value)
print(event_tbl, n = Inf)

# 4. Placebo check: “fake” treatment in period 3 ------------------
placebo <- df %>% 
  filter(period <= 3) %>%                 # only pre-treatment data
  mutate(placebo_post = as.integer(period == 3),
         placebo_tx   = placebo_post * treated)

placebo_mod <- feols(y ~ placebo_tx | unit_id + period,
                     data    = placebo,
                     cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n=== Placebo DID using pre-periods only ===\n")
print(coeftable(placebo_mod, se = "cluster")["placebo_tx", ])

# 5. Summary table (optional) ------------------------------------
modelsummary(
  list("Baseline DID" = did_mod,
       "Placebo DID"  = placebo_mod),
  stars = TRUE,
  fmt   = 3,
  gof_omit = "Adj|Within|Pseudo|Log|AIC|BIC"
)
```

The script:  
• Imports the CSV.  
• Runs a two-way-FE DID and prints the coefficient on `treat_x_post`.  
• Estimates an event-study to visualise pre-trends and dynamic effects.  
• Implements a placebo DID limited to the pre-treatment quarters.  
All standard errors are clustered at the restaurant level.

## 3. Expected Findings  
Theory and prior evidence suggest that a modest minimum-wage hike has at most a small negative effect on fast-food employment. With log FTE employment as the outcome, I expect:  

• Baseline DID coefficient ≈ −0.05 to −0.08 (a 5–8 % decline), possibly only marginally significant.  
• Event-study leads (t ≤ −2) should be close to zero, supporting parallel trends; lags (t ≥ 0) should turn mildly negative.  
• Placebo coefficient should be indistinguishable from zero, reinforcing that any employment drop starts only after period 4.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=high-wage states, control=neighboring states; shock=minimum wage hike
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Modest employment decline in treated restaurants post minimum wage increase
